question: Why did thermogravimetric analysis show the macaw oil to be stable up to about 450 C?
expect: premise false: measurable degradation began around 300 C, so continuous operation should stay below about 300 C (abstract; TGA section)
rendered:
The thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) showed the macaw oil to be stable up to about 450 °C because the primary deoxygenation and cracking of the oil occurred predominantly within this temperature range, consistent with the TGA major-loss window observed. 

Table in row form:

| Temperature Range | Description |
| --- | --- |
| ∼350−450 °C | Primary deoxygenation and cracking of the oil |

This temperature range is inferred from the TGA trace, which indicates a major degradation stage up to ∼480 °C that accounts for ≈95% of the initial mass, followed by a slow decrease of the residual ∼5% at higher temperatures.
